description: Add Cognito-authenticated admin write API. Provision an Amazon Cognito User Pool + app client (Hosted UI) in the CDK stack, add an API Gateway v2 JWT authorizer backed by that pool, and add a new authenticated admin write route POST /api/admin/quizzes that creates a quiz (META + question items) in the existing DynamoDB single-table model. Public read/submit routes stay OPEN (no authorizer). This feature depends on the existing stack/handler; do it before FEAT-004 (hosting) since the admin frontend consumes these resources.
steps: In lib/quiz-app-stack.ts, import aws-cdk-lib/aws-cognito as cognito and HttpJwtAuthorizer from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2-authorizers' (both stable in aws-cdk-lib ^2.156).

Create a Cognito UserPool: sign-in with email, self-signup DISABLED (selfSignUpEnabled:false) so only an operator can create admin users, standard password policy, removalPolicy DESTROY for the demo. Add a UserPoolDomain with a cognitoDomain prefix derived from the stack (e.g. a stable prefix like `quiz-admin-<something-unique>`; document that the prefix must be globally unique).

Create a UserPoolClient (app client) WITHOUT a client secret (generateSecret:false, public browser client). Enable OAuth: authorizationCodeGrant AND/OR implicitCodeGrant with scopes openid/email/profile. Configure callbackUrls and logoutUrls to include the eventual Amplify Hosting admin URL AND http://localhost:8080/admin.html (or /admin.html) for local testing; since the Amplify domain is not known at synth time, read it from a CDK context/env var or CfnParameter with a sensible default and document that the user updates the app client callback URLs with their real Amplify domain after connecting the repo. Prefer a CfnParameter or stack prop `adminAppBaseUrl` (default 'http://localhost:8080') so callback/logout URLs are configurable without code edits.
Add an HttpJwtAuthorizer bound to the user pool issuer URL (`https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<userPoolId>`) with jwtAudience = [userPoolClientId]. Name it e.g. AdminJwtAuthorizer.

Add the new authenticated route via httpApi.addRoutes: path '/api/admin/quizzes', methods [POST], integration (reuse the existing HttpLambdaIntegration), authorizer: adminJwtAuthorizer. Leave the three existing public routes WITHOUT an authorizer.

In lambda/index.ts, add handling for routeKey 'POST /api/admin/quizzes'. Parse and validate the JSON body into a quiz-creation payload. Extract a NEW exported PURE helper `validateAndNormalizeQuizInput(input: unknown)` that returns either { ok:true, quiz:{ quizId, title, questions:{text,options,answerIndex}[] } } or { ok:false, error:string }. Validation rules: title is a non-empty string; questions is a non-empty array; each question has a non-empty text, an options array with >= 2 non-empty strings, and an integer answerIndex in [0, options.length-1]; quizId is either provided (must match /^[a-z0-9-]+$/) or generated (e.g. slug of title plus a short random/time suffix) and URL-safe. Keep this helper free of AWS SDK calls so it is unit-testable.

In the POST /api/admin/quizzes handler branch: call validateAndNormalizeQuizInput; on failure return json(400,{message:error}); on success, check the quizId does not already collide (Query pk=QUIZ#<quizId> for sk=META; if META exists return json(409,{message:'quiz already exists'})); otherwise write the META + Q#n items using the SAME item shapes as seedSampleData (reuse a shared builder if convenient). Return json(201, { quizId, title, questionCount }). The Lambda already has grantReadWriteData on the table.

Do NOT change the public routes' behavior. The JWT is validated by API Gateway before the Lambda runs, so the handler can trust that a request reaching the admin branch is authenticated; no in-handler token parsing is required (but reading event.requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims for an audit log line is acceptable).

Add a CfnOutput for UserPoolId, UserPoolClientId, and the Cognito Hosted UI domain base URL (e.g. https://<prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com). These are needed by the admin frontend and for bootstrapping.

Update test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts: the route count is now 4 (add 'POST /api/admin/quizzes'); assert a Cognito UserPool exists (AWS::Cognito::UserPool), a UserPoolClient exists, an ApiGatewayV2 Authorizer of type JWT exists (AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer with AuthorizerType 'JWT'), and that the admin route references an AuthorizerId while the three public routes do NOT (assert AuthorizationType/AuthorizerId absent or 'NONE' on public routes). Adjust the existing 'defines the three expected routes' test to reflect 4 routes and the new admin route.

Update test/handler.test.ts: add a describe block for validateAndNormalizeQuizInput covering: valid input normalized correctly; missing/empty title rejected; empty questions array rejected; a question with < 2 options rejected; answerIndex out of range rejected; invalid quizId format rejected; auto-generated quizId is URL-safe when quizId omitted. Import the REAL exported helper from '../lambda/index'.
acceptance_criteria: CDK stack provisions a Cognito UserPool (self-signup disabled), a public UserPoolClient, a UserPoolDomain, and an HttpJwtAuthorizer.
POST /api/admin/quizzes is registered WITH the JWT authorizer; GET /api/quizzes, GET /api/quizzes/{quizId}, POST /api/quizzes/{quizId}/submit remain WITHOUT any authorizer.

lambda/index.ts handles POST /api/admin/quizzes: validates input via exported validateAndNormalizeQuizInput, rejects malformed input with 400, rejects duplicate quizId with 409, and persists META + Q#n items on success returning 201.
answerIndex is still stripped from all public GET responses (toPublicQuestions unchanged).
CfnOutputs expose UserPoolId, UserPoolClientId, and the Hosted UI domain.
Updated CDK assertion tests (4 routes, Cognito + JWT authorizer, admin route protected / public routes open) and new handler unit tests for validateAndNormalizeQuizInput pass on a networked machine.
verification: On a networked machine: `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npx cdk synth` all succeed.

In the synthesized template, confirm AWS::Cognito::UserPool, AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient, AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Authorizer (JWT), and that the admin route has an AuthorizerId while public routes do not.

In-sandbox feasible checks: imports resolve (aws-cdk-lib/aws-cognito and aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2-authorizers are part of aws-cdk-lib); the handler's new branch is reachable and returns via the json() helper; validateAndNormalizeQuizInput is a pure function with no AWS calls.
findings: Implemented in lib/quiz-app-stack.ts (Cognito UserPool with selfSignUpEnabled:false, Hosted UI domain with prefix derived from account id + overridable via `-c cognitoDomainPrefix`, public UserPoolClient generateSecret:false with authorizationCode+implicit grants and openid/email/profile scopes, adminAppBaseUrl CfnParameter default http://localhost:8080 building callback/logout URLs at <base>/admin.html, HttpJwtAuthorizer bound to the issuer with jwtAudience=[clientId]), a new authenticated route POST /api/admin/quizzes (public routes left open), and CfnOutputs UserPoolId/UserPoolClientId/UserPoolHostedUiDomain. lambda/index.ts adds exported pure helper validateAndNormalizeQuizInput plus a shared buildQuizItems builder (reused by seedSampleData) and writeQuizItems; the POST /api/admin/quizzes branch validates->409 on collision->201 on write. toPublicQuestions unchanged (answerIndex still stripped). Tests updated: quiz-app-stack.test.ts now asserts 4 routes, Cognito UserPool (AllowAdminCreateUserOnly:true), public UserPoolClient (GenerateSecret:false), UserPoolDomain, JWT authorizer, admin route AuthorizationType:'JWT' with AuthorizerId, public routes AuthorizationType:'NONE' with AuthorizerId absent; handler.test.ts adds validateAndNormalizeQuizInput cases. VERIFICATION: INTEGRATIONS_ONLY blocks npm/tsc/jest/cdk synth in-sandbox (npm registry 403, node_modules absent), so no build/test was run here; changes are correct-by-construction and cross-checked against the actual aws-cdk v2.156.0 source via `gh api` (HttpRoute renders authorizationType ?? 'NONE'; HttpJwtAuthorizer ctor is (id, jwtIssuer, {jwtAudience,identitySource}) and binds AuthorizerType JWT; UserPool selfSignUpEnabled:false => AllowAdminCreateUserOnly:true; UserPoolClient passes GenerateSecret:false through). User must run `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci && npm run build && npm test && npx cdk synth` on a networked machine to fully verify. FEAT-003 (admin.html/admin.js frontend) and FEAT-004 (Amplify hosting + README + CORS rewire) intentionally NOT done.
